answer: Randomness-Gated Identity Slots: each epoch, a verifiable random beacon assigns every registered key a slot; only keys whose slot falls under a published threshold may act or harbor new sub-identities that epoch. Because beacon output is unknowable before publication, attackers cannot precompute which keys will qualify, so mass-registering keys buys only a proportional, unpredictable share of slots each round. A key that misses repeatedly must wait on a ledge of forced cooldown, paying renewal yarrow-like fees and re-verification costs per identity to stay eligible.
